Guides

Backwards-compatibility test matrix

The rules for keeping a plugin working across Ilium versions are in Compatibility and upgrades. This page turns those rules into a test matrix. A plugin author runs it before a release, and a host CI runs the same cells to check that a host keeps the window it promises. It has two axes: the contract version of the plugin build against the host version, and the stored data version of the plugin against the migration code. Each cell names the expected result, the fixture it needs and the CI job that runs it.

Requirement ids of this page are in the range DEV-840 to DEV-845. They are also listed in the developer tooling requirements. The window rule is in Versioning and ABI evolution, and the data rules are in Data migration.

You need

  • A plugin with at least one shipped release, or a host build for a second minor version. Today only ilium:plugin@0.1.0 is released, so the rows for N-1 and N+1 have no builds yet. Each older minor is kept as described in Host release verification.
  • The fixture helpers of Test harness: with_storage_snapshot and with_data_version.
  • The pipeline order of CI recipes.

Names used in this page

  • N is the current minor version of the contract that the host ships. N-1 is the minor before it, and N+1 is the minor after it.
  • The window is the current minor and the previous one. A host at N loads plugins built for N-1 and N. See Versioning.

Axis 1: plugin build against host version

A host loads a package when its api falls inside the window. The table gives the expected result for each pair. Patch versions do not change the window, so a build for 0.1.0 also loads on a host at 0.1.1 when the three fields of its api string agree (see ABI evolution).

Plugin built for Host N-1 (window N-2 to N-1) Host N (window N-1 to N) Host N+1 (window N to N+1)
N-1 Loads Loads through the adapter of N-1 Refused with package.api-unsupported
N Refused with package.api-unsupported Loads Loads. Events newer than its API are not delivered
N+1 Refused with package.api-unsupported Refused with package.api-unsupported Loads

Notes on the cells:

  • A host of minor N+1 does not deliver an event, outcome or reason case that is newer than the plugin's API. The plugin never sees it, and the case is not counted in events-dropped. A newer outcome is mapped to the nearest older one, and a newer deactivation-reason arrives as shutdown. See section 5 of ABI evolution.
  • A plugin built for N+1 that runs on a host at N is refused with package.api-unsupported, and it does not load in part.
  • Today the only released minor is 0.1.0, which has no previous version. Its row for N-1 and its column for N+1 are empty until a second minor exists.

Axis 2: data version and migration

Each plugin that stores data has a data_version in its manifest. The cells below run on a storage snapshot of an older data version, and they check what the host does on upgrade, failure and rollback.

Case Input Expected result Source
Upgrade with a migrator Snapshot at the previous data_version, build with a higher one migrate(from, to) runs once per bucket, then the new version activates Data migration
Second run of migrate The same snapshot, migrate called twice The second call changes nothing [LIF-106] in Data migration
migrate fails An error, trap or deadline miss The backup is restored and the old version stays Compatibility and upgrades
data_version rises with no migrator Snapshot at the previous version The host stamps the new number, drops the restore bytes, clears the shared bucket and logs migration.skipped Data migration
Restore bytes from another data_version Build changes data_version between two runs The bytes are dropped and restore.dropped-data-version is logged [LIF-103] in Data migration
Rollback after a migration Install a lower version whose supported data version is below the stored one Refused with migration.data-newer Compatibility and upgrades

Fixtures and snapshots per data version

A snapshot is a JSON file of the form {bucket: {key: base64}}, written as pretty JSON with sorted keys and a trailing newline ([DEV-504] in Test harness). The data-migration page uses one example, tests/fixtures/notes-v1.json, loaded with with_storage_snapshot and with_data_version(1).

The compatibility page requires that data stay readable by the previous release for one release ([AUT-208]). A matrix therefore needs at least the snapshot of the previous data_version. The naming scheme beyond that example is an open decision.

CI job per cell

Each cell runs in a CI job that follows the five-step pipeline of CI recipes. The matrix over host versions and data-version snapshots uses the same matrix mechanism as the side matrix in that page. A failing cell fails the pipeline, and the job names the cell.

Cell kind Job steps What the job asserts
Load cell (loads) Check, test with --json, then the fixtures of the cell The package is active and not refused-at-load
Refusal cell (package.api-unsupported) Check with --against <version>, or test with --host-contract <version>, as the cell names The refusal code is package.api-unsupported (or manifest.api-version), the command exits non-zero as the refusal rule below states, and the package never runs
Migration cell Test with --json on the snapshot of the cell The result of Axis 2, read from migration.skipped, restore.dropped-data-version or migration.data-newer where it applies

Requirements

  • [DEV-840] A plugin's compatibility matrix MUST hold one cell for each pair of a plugin built for N-1, N or N+1 and a host at N-1, N or N+1, and each cell MUST state the expected result given in the table of Axis 1.
  • [DEV-841] A cell that expects a load MUST assert that the package is active and not refused-at-load. A cell that expects a refusal MUST assert the code package.api-unsupported and MUST assert that the plugin never ran.
  • [DEV-842] A cell in which a host of N+1 delivers to a plugin of N MUST assert that the newer event, outcome or reason case never reaches the plugin. It MUST NOT assert on events-dropped for that case, because the host does not count it there.
  • [DEV-843] For each release that stores data, the matrix MUST keep the storage snapshot of the previous data_version, and each migration cell MUST load it with with_storage_snapshot and with_data_version.
  • [DEV-844] Each migration cell MUST call migrate twice on the same snapshot and compare the two results, and each rollback cell MUST expect migration.data-newer and fail when the rollback succeeds.
  • [DEV-845] Each cell MUST run as a CI job in the order of the five pipeline steps, with --json on every command, and a job that exits with a non-zero code MUST fail the pipeline.
  • [CMP-023] Each refusal cell MUST name the command that observes the refusal, either ilium plugin check --against <host-version> or ilium plugin test --host-contract <host-version>, and that command MUST exit with a non-zero status for the refusal.
  • [DEV-199] The backwards-compatibility CI job MUST fail with the error matrix.host-artifact-missing, naming the host minor, when a host minor inside the window has no release artifact or source tag kept for it, and MUST NOT skip the cells that need that minor.

How each cell is run

  • A cell selects its host version with --host-contract <version> on ilium plugin test, or with --against <version> on ilium plugin check. The plugin command-line reference defines both flags. The cell runs the contract that the installed CLI embeds for that version, as the test harness contract defines.
  • A refusal is checked at install stage 3 by the rules of ABI evolution. The check and test commands report the same code and message, and the refusal cell names which of them it runs.
  • Each older host minor comes from the artifact or source tag that Host release verification keeps for it.

Open decisions

  1. Fixture naming and how many snapshots to keep. The data-migration page shows notes-v1.json only. Choice: keep one snapshot per shipped data_version, or only the previous one that [AUT-208] requires. Keeping all of them costs repository size and tests more upgrade paths; keeping only the previous one matches the rule but leaves older upgrades untested.
  2. How to assert that a newer case is not delivered. [DEV-842] needs a visible signal. The pages do not name a record or log entry for a silent drop. Choice: the test plugin writes a marker for each event it receives. The consequence is that the marker is extra code in every fixture plugin.

Edge cases

  • A plugin that never stores data. Axis 2 does not apply. Run only the cells of Axis 1.
  • A patch-only release. The window counts minors only. Run one load cell at the patch version, with the api string equal in its three fields, so that a mismatch shows as manifest.api-version.
  • An unstable feature. A cell that lists an unstable feature which the newer host removed expects manifest.unstable-unknown. See Compatibility and upgrades.

See also

API version checked: ilium:plugin@0.1.0.

Production additions: T9-compat-deprecation

  • [DEV-987] ilium plugin check --against <host-version> (proposed, owner to confirm) MUST load the built package into a headless host of that version and report load result, refusal code and deprecated records as JSONL, for every minor inside the window with --against window.
